title: introduce-release-notes-playbook-and-metadata-scenarios
author: Maya Desai
release_notes: Adds a release-notes playbook that synthesizes human-friendly changelog entries from model metadata diffs and perf-profile deltas; includes templates, a scenario engine, and a lightweight preview UI in the curation dashboard. Backward compatible; opt-in via registry.config.playbook.enabled.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a Release Notes Playbook for the model registry: a small, opinionated engine that converts structured model onboarding metadata and performance-profile deltas into concise, human-readable changelog seeds. The goal is to reduce manual work for release authors and provide consistent impact statements for model rollouts.

Motivation: We routinely see messy hand-authored release notes when models are onboarded or updated. The model metadata (tags, affinity, quantization profile) and perf profile deltas (latency P50/P95, memory/per-token cost changes) already contain signal that can be translated to release-notes bullets. This PR codifies a scenario-driven mapping ("playbook") so release notes are: 1) consistent, 2) traceable to metadata diffs, and 3) suggest rollout hints (canary size, recommended fallback).

What this change does: 1) Adds a playbook engine (registry/playbook/) that consumes: a) model metadata diff (onboard vs previous variant), b) performance profile delta JSON, c) optional curated annotations from reviewers. 2) Implements a scenario classifier that emits a prioritized list of changelog seeds: "Performance improvement", "Increased memory use — consider lower batch sizes", "Model variant renamed/alias added", "Precision/quantization change with expected quality trade-off". 3) Adds template rendering with short and long variants and localization-ready strings. 4) Exposes a preview endpoint and a small React component in the curation UI so SREs/PMs can review and edit seeds before publishing. 5) Hooks into the existing release-assembler pipeline to optionally attach generated seeds as suggested release notes.

Implementation notes: - Core engine implemented in TypeScript (registry/playbook/*.ts). Lightweight rules defined as ordered scenarios with guard predicates and priority scoring. - Performance-profile normalizer added (registry/profiles/normalizer.ts) to compute delta buckets for latency, cost, and memory across workload slices. - Preview UI lives under redwood-model-registry/ui/components/PlaybookPreview.tsx and calls /api/playbook/preview. - Feature gated by registry.config.playbook.enabled (default: false) and opt-in per-model via model.annotations.playbook: true. - Adds unit tests for scenario matching and end-to-end integration tests for preview and assembly (tests/playbook/*).

Checklist: - [x] Scenario engine and core templates implemented - [x] Preview API + UI component - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs: developer guide + sample playbook rules - [x] Linear tickets linked - [x] Feature gate with safe default (disabled)

High-level commits: - 73d2f9a: initial playbook engine and scenario DSL - af1b2c4: add performance-profile normalizer and delta buckets - e8c0b1d: wire preview API + React component - bb3a9d2: add tests and fixtures for sample model diffs - 4c6e2b5: docs and upgrade notes, add feature gate

Files changed (high level): - registry/playbook/engine.ts - registry/playbook/scenarios/*.ts - registry/profiles/normalizer.ts - ui/components/PlaybookPreview.tsx - api/routes/playbook.ts - tests/playbook/* - docs/dev/playbook.md - migrations/add_playbook_flag.sql - samples/fixtures/profile-deltas/sample-2025-10.json

Review conversation (selected): - Liam O'Neal (review): "Nice direction. Two requests: (1) concretely show how scoring prioritizes multiple overlapping scenarios (e.g., latency drop + quantization) and (2) ensure we never auto-publish seeds without an explicit curator approval step."

- Maya (author): "Reply: added an ordered 'priority' field to each scenario and explicit 'requiresApproval' flag; playbook.preview returns a 'publishable' boolean that the UI interprets. Updated tests to cover overlap resolution."

- Sofia Ramirez (review): "API looks good. Suggestion: for the preview endpoint, return deterministic IDs for seeds so UI edits can be diffed and reconciled across retries."

- Maya: "Added seed-id stable hashing based on (model_id, variant, scenario_key, commit_hash) — documented in dev notes."

- Jordan Kim (review): "Please add a fallback when perf profile delta buckets are missing (e.g., newly onboarded models with no baseline). We should still generate alias/metadata change notes."

- Maya: "Handled: if no baseline we fall back to 'first-release' scenario and avoid perf assertions; tests included."

CI and checks: - Unit tests: pass - Integration (playbook preview + assembly): pass - Lint: pass - Docs build: pass - Canary E2E (sample fixture): pass All checks green on the final run.

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Default off via feature gate. Registry operators can enable per-tenant. When enabled, generated seeds are suggestions only; publishing requires a curator action from the UI or an explicit API call with curator signature. No breaking changes to existing registry contracts.

Upgrade notes for operators: - Run migrations/add_playbook_flag.sql to add feature flag toggles. - Optional: populate sample playbook rules at registry.playbook.rulesPath or use built-in defaults. - Recommended rollout: enable in staging, exercise with 5 recent model deltas, review generated seeds, then enable in production for one team first.

Merge: Squash merge into main after approvals from Liam and Sofia. Changelog: Added release notes playbook and preview UI; feature disabled by default.

Contact and follow-ups: - For follow-up work: ENG-1689 (improve multilingual templates), PM-402 (UX polish for curator workflow). If we observe noisy suggestions in canary, plan follow-up to add higher-threshold heuristics and sampling controls.
